name: Salvia divinorum
warning: Heavy uses hard stepped motion, recursive re-tiling and ~7 s page-turn flips. May be disorienting. Photosensitivity note applies.
tierNotes: Threshold: faint lateral lean — the field is dragged sideways along a curved seam (early sway + low seamPull); scene otherwise intact.
Light: the seam pull is clear; the very first mirror fold begins to wake (foldTile ramps from ~0.26 intensity).
Common: visible recursive re-tiling — the scene folds into a couple of mirrored copies of itself around the cursor — plus the constant sideways pull; still legible as this room.

Strong: louder, larger fold stack (copies-of-copies) taking up more of the frame, deeper zoom; the vivid cartoon remap begins (realityBreak ramps from 0.70) so it stays lively, not washed; ~7 s page-turn rolls the whole tiling over; time steps toward ~11 fps.

Heavy: reality break — the fold-tiled scene is remapped through a loud vivid cartoon palette (image-derived from the scene's own luminance, not a pasted overlay); the original photo is gone. Comparable in force to DMT breakthrough, in salvia's own re-tiling idiom. The kaleidoscope centre tracks the mouse.
